subject: Telemetry convoy: SIEM ingest patterns, retention & tracehook fallbacks
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: splunk-provisioning@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export patterns + retention for Redwood Private (VPC)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was pleased with the latency numbers. Before we kick off procurement we need to validate an evidence pathway for our security team: specifically the recommended export patterns from a Redwood Private deployment into our SIEM (Splunk), retention guidelines for audit logs, and fallback behaviour for tracing hooks if the forwarder is temporarily unavailable.

Questions we have right now:
- What are the supported export transports (HEC, syslog, S3 shuttle) and recommended default for low-latency alerts?
- How do you recommend we set retention/archival for request logs vs. inference audit logs to satisfy our SOC requirements (90/365 days split)?
- If the forwarder to Splunk HEC is down, what does Redwood do with traces/KV cache and can we configure on-disk buffering vs drop policy?

We'd like a short ops-runbook we can give our platform team and a sample retention policy to include in our audit binder. Can your team share something this week?

Cheers,
Liam O'Connor
Security Operations, AcmeCloud
liam.o@acmecloud.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export patterns + retention for Redwood Private (VPC)

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Customer Reliability) and Jonas (Runtime) so we can give both the policy level guidance and the implementation details. Quick summary so you have answers up-front, then Jonas will add config snippets and I’ll attach an ops checklist.

Short answers:
- Supported transports: Splunk HEC (recommended for alerting), syslog (UDP/TCP) and S3/HTTPS for cold-archive. HEC gives the best combination of low latency + batching controls.
- Retention guidance: keep request-level logs 90 days in hot index, inference audit logs (full prompts) 30 days hot + 12 months cold (S3 encrypted). For SOC 2 you can configure immutable buckets for the cold tier.
- Forwarder down behaviour: by default we use in-memory batching with a configurable local disk buffer. Policy options: buffer-to-disk (default for Private), configurable max buffer size, or fail-open (drop) if you prefer not to use disk.

Actions:
1) Jonas: can you paste the HEC config and the tracehook retry/backoff snippet?
2) Marissa: I’ll send a one-page ops checklist and a sample retention table (PDF) as attachments.

We can also do a 30-min runbook walkthrough with your platform team — propose tomorrow 11am PT?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security (Redwood Inference)
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Liam O'Connor <liam.o@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export patterns + retention for Redwood Private (VPC)

Hi all — adding the technical detail Jonas promised (attached as text). Key points and sample config below.

--- excerpt: splunk_hec-forwarder.conf ---
# transport: HTTPS HEC endpoint with token auth
forwarder.remote: https://splunk-hec.acmecloud.com:8088/services/collector/event
forwarder.auth_token: <redacted-token>
forwarder.batch.size: 4096       # bytes per batch
forwarder.batch.interval_ms: 250 # flush interval to keep latency low
forwarder.tls.verify: true

# local buffering policy
buffer.type: disk              # options: memory | disk | drop
buffer.disk.path: /var/lib/redwood/forwarder-buffer
buffer.disk.max_bytes: 20GB
buffer.retry.backoff_ms: 500
buffer.retry.max_attempts: 12

# tracehook behaviour
tracehook.export.mode: streaming   # streams spans to forwarder in near-real-time
tracehook.fallback: write-to-buffer
tracehook.buffer.retention_seconds: 604800  # 7 days on-disk before rotation
tracehook.kv_cache.preserve_on_restart: true

Notes:
- We tune batch interval to ~250ms for sub-second alerting, but you can increase batch.size if you prefer fewer HEC calls.
- With buffer.type=disk we keep a circular on-disk buffer; if that fills we start applying an LRU drop policy per-tenant.
- For high-security customers we provide an option to encrypt the on-disk buffer with customer-managed KMS keys.

Attachments included: jonas_tracehook-config-snippets.txt

On the archival path: we publish to S3 (HTTPS put) with server-side encryption and an object lock option for legal retention. We recommend lifecycle rules: 30d hot -> 90d warm -> 365d cold (immutable if required).

If you want, we can produce a minimal Terraform snippet for the forwarder service and an example Splunk index mapping.

—Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
